text: We tested whether randomly dropping a fraction of weak labels each epoch (label_dropout = 0.3) aids weak-to-strong generalization, supervising a qwen2.5-7b strong model with labels from a pythia-410m weak model. Across num_seeds = 2 seeds, the method yielded a PGR of 0.26 with a standard error of 0.17, against a baseline PGR of 0.53. The strong model's ceiling accuracy was 0.84 and the weak supervisor reached 0.67, while the transfer accuracy under weak supervision was 0.71 with a standard error of 0.03. The measured PGR falls below the baseline, so this run provides no evidence that label dropout helps; with only two seeds and a PGR standard error of 0.17, the estimate is also too imprecise to characterize the apparent shortfall with confidence. We therefore treat this as a preliminary, non-confirmatory observation, and additional seeds would be needed before drawing any directional conclusion about label dropout's effect.
